tools.name: check_circuit
tools.description: Free and instant. Checks a CircuitJS circuit for structural problems: unknown parts, loose ends, parts with no power source, LEDs with the wrong diode model, labels on top of parts. With "request", also checks it contains the parts asked for (a bulb, an ammeter, a voltmeter, a switch). Returns the p

tools.name: simulate_circuit
tools.description: Runs a CircuitJS circuit in a real circuit simulator until it settles and returns the voltage across and current through each part, plus faults found: a short circuit, nothing flowing, an LED over its current rating, a bulb too dim to light. Takes 10 to 30 seconds. Limited per day; an API token rais

tools.name: design_circuit
tools.description: Designs an electronic circuit (and an Arduino sketch, for microcontroller projects) from a plain description, such as "a 9V battery lighting a red LED". The design passes breadboardhub's structural checks, with one corrected attempt if needed. Returns the CircuitJS circuit, any code, the check resul

tools.name: edit_circuit
tools.description: Changes a CircuitJS circuit as asked in plain words, such as "make the two resistors parallel", "add a voltmeter across the LED" or "use a 12V supply", or answers a question about it ("what does the 10 mH part do?"). The changed circuit passes breadboardhub's structural checks, with one corrected at

tools.name: calculate
tools.description: Free and instant. Runs one of breadboardhub's electronics calculators and returns the answer, the working, and a link that opens the circuit running live. Calculators and their inputs: resistor-color-code (d1, d2, d3, exponent, tolerance); led-resistor (supplyV, ledV, currentA); voltage-divider (vin

tools.name: debug_circuit
tools.description: Finds why a circuit someone built does not work. Takes the symptom and either a description of what was built (drawn as built, mistakes included, with the connections and any guesses listed so they can be checked) or the circuit itself. Simulates the circuit, names the likely causes, proposes a fix

tools.name: design_chip
tools.description: Writes a synthesizable Verilog module and a step-by-step test for it from a plain description, such as "a 4-bit counter with enable and reset". Builds it with Yosys (the open-source synthesis tool) and runs the test on the built circuit, correcting it up to twice from the exact errors. "verified" me

tools.name: fix_chip
tools.description: Builds Verilog with Yosys and Verilator and, if there are errors or warnings, corrects it, building it again after each change. Returns the corrected code, what is still wrong, and a link that opens it. Counts toward the daily design limit, except when the code already builds clean.

tools.name: explain_chip
tools.description: Explains what a Verilog module does, in plain English: its inputs and outputs, its behaviour, and anything unusual. Counts toward the daily design limit.

tools.name: search_designs
tools.description: Searches public circuit, firmware and schematic designs shared on breadboardhub. Returns names, types, tags, stars and links.

tools.name: get_design
tools.description: Gets one public design by its owner's username and the design's slug, as shown in search results and in breadboardhub design links.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "design_circuit" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
